message.content:
Here’s a mix of classic, modern, and cult‑favorite horror films you might enjoy:

| Year | Title | Why it’s worth watching |
|------|-------|------------------------|
| 1960 | **Psycho** (Alfred Hitchcock) | A masterclass in suspense and psychological terror. |
| 1968 | **Night of the Living Dead** (George A. Romero) | The original zombie film that changed the genre. |
| 1974 | **The Exorcist** | A chilling story of demonic possession that still feels fresh. |
| 1978 | **Halloween** (John Carpenter) | The quintessential slasher with a haunting score. |
| 1980 | **The Shining** (Stanley Kubrick) | A psychological horror that blends supernatural dread with isolation. |
| 1984 | **A Nightmare on Elm Street** (Wes Craven) | Freddy Krueger’s nightmare‑inducing terror is iconic. |
| 1991 | **The Silence of the Lambs** | A tense thriller featuring Hannibal Lecter and Clarice Starling. |
| 1999 | **The Blair Witch Project** | Found‑footage horror that made audiences feel like they were there. |
| 2002 | **28 Days Later** (Danny Boyle) | A fast‑moving, post‑apocalyptic zombie film with a strong emotional core. |
| 2004 | **Saw** | A psychological thriller that introduced a new kind of horror puzzle. |
| 2007 | **Paranormal Activity** | Low‑budget found‑footage film that sparked a whole franchise. |
| 2010 | **The Conjuring** (James Wan) | A modern supernatural horror that blends scares with a compelling narrative. |
| 2012 | **The Cabin in the Woods** | A meta‑take on horror tropes that’s both funny and frightening. |
| 2014 | **It Follows** | A unique premise that turns everyday life into a nightmare. |
| 2015 | **The Witch** | A slow‑burning, atmospheric horror set in 1630s New England. |
| 2017 | **Get Out** (Jordan Peele) | A socially conscious horror that’s as smart as it is scary. |
| 2018 | **A Quiet Place** (John Krasinski) | Silence is the key to survival in this tense, family‑driven horror. |
| 2019 | **Midsommar** (Ari Aster) | A daylight horror that’s unsettling in its own bright way. |
| 2020 | **The Invisible Man** (Eliseo Subiela) | A modern retelling of a classic horror story. |
| 2021 | **Candyman** (Nia DaCosta) | A fresh take on a horror legend with strong social commentary. |
| 2022 | **The Black Phone** (Scott Derrickson) | A supernatural thriller that’s both creepy and emotionally resonant. |
| 2023 | **M3GAN** (David Gordon Green) | A horror‑comedy about a murderous AI doll that’s oddly entertaining. |

Feel free to pick any era or style that suits your mood—whether you want a psychological thriller, a supernatural scare, or a slasher classic. Enjoy the chills!
